ai.description: *Uropeltis madurensis* is a small, cylindrical snake reaching 20–30 cm. It is dark brown with yellow lateral spots and possesses a truncated, shield-like tail tip used for burrowing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis madurensis* is best distinguished by its uniquely truncated, shield-like tail ending in a distinct, bicarinate (two-ridged) terminal scale.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis madurensis* inhabits the high-altitude montane shola forests and grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Madura earth snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through loose soil to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis madurensis* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis madurensis* is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and shola forests of the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, India.
